title: Predictors of Successful Conservative Rehabilitation Following Radical Prostatectomy: A Prospective Cohort Study
summary:
After surgical removal of the prostate due to prostate cancer (radical prostatectomy), many men experience involuntary urine leakage (urinary incontinence). This condition can significantly affect their quality of life. Rehabilitation measures, particularly pelvic floor muscle training, can help improve bladder control over time. However, the recovery process varies considerably between patients.

The aim of this study is to identify personal and medical factors that may influence how quickly patients regain urinary control after prostate surgery. Factors such as age, body weight, type of surgery, preservation of nerves during surgery, and the initial severity of urinary incontinence will be examined.

Approximately 200 men experiencing urinary incontinence after radical prostatectomy will participate in the study while undergoing a standard three-week inpatient rehabilitation program at Cecilien Klinik in Bad Lippspringe, Germany.

At the beginning of rehabilitation, medical information and details about urinary incontinence will be collected. All participants will receive the clinic's usual rehabilitation program, including pelvic floor muscle training and other physiotherapy measures. Participation in the study will not affect their regular medical treatment.

After discharge, participants will be contacted every two weeks for six months, primarily by email and, if necessary, by telephone. During these contacts, they will be asked how many incontinence pads they currently use per day. This information will help determine when and to what extent urinary control improves.

Participation is voluntary, and no additional experimental treatments will be performed. The findings may help healthcare professionals better predict recovery after prostate surgery and provide more individualized advice and treatment in the future.

interventions.name: Prospective cohort of adult male patients with urinary incontinence following radical prostatectomy who undergo a standardized three-week conservative inpatient rehabilitation program at Cecilien Klinik, including pelvic floor muscle training, ergometer training, and other physiotherapeutic measures

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male patients following radical prostatectomy.
- Presence of postoperative urinary incontinence.
- Participation in conservative inpatient rehabilitation at Cecilien Klinik in Bad Lippspringe, Germany.
- Written informed consent following appropriate patient information.
- Availability via email and/or telephone for follow-up assessments over six months after discharge.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Neurological disorders affecting bladder function (e.g., Parkinson's disease or multiple sclerosis).
2. Pre-existing severe urinary incontinence of another etiology.
3. Incomplete or missing clinical data.
4. Inability to participate in the conservative rehabilitation program.
5. Absence of written informed consent for study participation.
